findings.title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so team admins are incorrectly denied
findings.body: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, ...)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, ...))`. The `&&` means a user must be BOTH an admin and an owner of the booking's team. A team admin who is not the owner (the common case for teams with a separate owner) fails this check and gets a FORBIDDEN error unless they happen to also be the organizer or an attendee, even though the check is clearly meant to allow either role (the name says 'Or'). The condition should use `||`.

findings.title: EventManager is constructed with the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: The handler explicitly allows any attendee of the booking to add guests (`isAttendee` check passes), but then builds `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` from `ctx.user` (the requester) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. When the requester is an attendee rather than the organizer, the EventManager runs with the attendee's calendar credentials, which do not own the calendar event for this booking — the calendar update will fail or be attempted against the wrong account. The EventManager should be constructed from the booking's organizer (`booking.user`) and their credentials, not the requesting user.

findings.title: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is bypassable via letter case
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased when parsed (`email.toLowerCase()`), but the guest emails being tested are not: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. An email like `Spam@Example.com` will not match a blacklisted `spam@example.com`, so the blacklist is trivially bypassed by changing the case of any character. The same case-sensitivity applies to the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email`, so `Alice@Example.com` can be added when `alice@example.com` is already an attendee. Both comparisons should lowercase the guest email first.

findings.title: No check on booking status — guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
findings.body: The handler fetches the booking and only checks the requester's identity; it never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`. A user can add guests (and trigger calendar updates plus emails to every attendee) for a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking, which is nonsensical and confusing to recipients. The query/authorization block should reject bookings whose status is not ACCEPTED (or at minimum not CANCELLED/REJECTED), and consider whether adding guests to already-ended bookings should be allowed.

findings.title: No upper bound on the number of guests — email-bombing / spam vector
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max(...)` limit. Any authorized user (including any attendee of a booking, per the handler's permission check) can submit thousands of emails in one request. Each request causes `createMany` of that many attendee rows and, via `sendAddGuestsEmails`, an email to every existing attendee plus a 'scheduled' email to every new 'guest'. This is a trivially abusable mass-email/spam vector (the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env var only helps if pre-configured). Add a sane maximum to the schema.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests list
findings.body: The handler carefully computes `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already on the booking and blacklisted ones) but then calls `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original, unfiltered input. Any email in the request that was already an attendee (and thus filtered out of the DB write) still appears in `newGuests`, so in `sendAddGuestsEmails` that existing attendee matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` — a duplicate 'booking scheduled' email — instead of the intended guests-added notification. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: New-guest detection in sendAddGuestsEmails is case-sensitive
findings.body: `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares emails with exact string matching, but email addresses are case-insensitive in practice and are stored/normalized inconsistently. If the guest email supplied by the user differs in case from the value written to the attendees table (or vice versa), a newly added guest will be misclassified and receive the 'guests added' notification meant for existing attendees rather than their own 'scheduled' email (which contains their join details as a new participant). Normalize both sides to lowercase before comparing.

findings.title: Caught error is swallowed with a console.log that omits the error object
findings.body: The `catch (err)` around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only logs the constant string `"Error sending AddGuestsEmails"` — `err` is never logged, so email delivery failures (bad SMTP config, template rendering errors, etc.) are completely undiagnosable in production while the handler still returns success ("Guests added"). At minimum log the error (ideally via the project logger, not console.log).

findings.title: isInvalidEmail error state is never cleared on retry
findings.body: When validation fails, `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` shows the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error. But the flag is only reset by the Cancel button or a successful mutation. If the user corrects the emails and clicks Add again, the request is sent while the stale error message remains visible until the dialog closes, and if the dialog is reopened via the menu (without Cancel), the previous error is still shown. Clear `isInvalidEmail(false)` at the start of `handleAdd` (or when the value changes / dialog opens).

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests handler, schema, or permission logic
findings.body: This PR adds a new tRPC mutation with non-trivial authorization (organizer vs. attendee vs. team admin/owner), blacklist filtering, deduplication against existing attendees, DB writes, calendar updates, and email fan-out — but includes no unit or integration tests. The kinds of bugs present in this diff (the `&&` vs `||` in the team check, the case-sensitive blacklist comparison, passing `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`) are exactly what a handler test exercising each permission path and filtering rule would have caught. Tests should cover: each allowed/denied role, duplicate attendee emails, blacklisted emails (including mixed case), and non-ACCEPTED booking statuses.
